brief.title: Global Fuel Price Trends & Policy Impact Analysis (2020–2026)
brief.one_liner: A comprehensive trend analysis of retail fuel prices across 84 countries, examining the interplay between Brent Crude benchmarks, taxation, subsidies, and regional economic conditions over a six-year period.
brief.goal: Equip energy policy analysts with a clear understanding of how global crude oil price movements translate into retail fuel costs across different regions, income levels, and subsidy regimes — and identify where policy interventions have been most and least effective at stabilizing consumer prices.

required_sections.title: Global Fuel Price Overview
required_sections.objective: Present high-level summary statistics for petrol, diesel, and LPG prices across the full 2020–2026 period, including overall averages, ranges, and the trajectory of Brent Crude as a baseline.

required_sections.title: Temporal Price Trends & Volatility
required_sections.objective: Analyze weekly and yearly price trends for each fuel type, identify periods of peak volatility (e.g., COVID-19 demand shock, 2022 energy crisis), and quantify the correlation between Brent Crude movements and retail price changes.

required_sections.title: Regional Price Disparities
required_sections.objective: Compare average fuel prices across the seven geographic regions, highlighting which regions consistently pay the most and least, and how regional spreads have evolved over time.

required_sections.title: Impact of Subsidies and Taxation on Retail Prices
required_sections.objective: Evaluate how subsidy levels (High vs. Low) and tax percentages influence the retail price consumers pay, segmented by income level. Assess whether high-subsidy countries show lower price pass-through from crude oil fluctuations.

required_sections.title: Fuel Affordability by Income Level
required_sections.objective: Segment countries by income classification (High, Middle, Low) and analyze differences in fuel pricing, tax burden, and price stability to draw conclusions about energy equity.

required_sections.title: Key Findings & Policy Implications
required_sections.objective: Synthesize the most important insights from the analysis into actionable findings, including recommendations for policymakers on subsidy design, tax calibration, and price stabilization mechanisms.

kpis.name: Average Retail Petrol Price (USD/Liter)
kpis.description: The mean petrol price across all countries and weeks, used as the primary benchmark for global fuel cost.

kpis.name: Brent-to-Retail Price Correlation
kpis.description: Pearson correlation coefficient between weekly Brent Crude prices and retail petrol/diesel prices, measuring how tightly global benchmarks drive local costs.

kpis.name: Subsidy Price Dampening Effect
kpis.description: The percentage difference in average retail fuel price between High-subsidy and Low-subsidy countries, quantifying the impact of government intervention.

kpis.name: Regional Price Spread
kpis.description: The difference between the highest and lowest regional average petrol price in a given year, indicating global pricing inequality.

kpis.name: Tax-to-Price Ratio by Income Level
kpis.description: Average tax percentage segmented by income level, revealing how fiscal policy on fuel varies with national wealth.
